# Differences from the original MSX-MIDI BASIC extension

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../diff-from-msxmidi.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

This document covers only **the differences from the original MSX-MIDI BASIC extension**. For the full specification of the statements and MML, see [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

The MML language itself is the same as in the original MSX-MIDI BASIC extension; what it plays and the machine it runs on are different. There are five kinds of differences.

| | |
|---|---|
| [The sound sources and channels are different](#the-sound-sources-and-channels-are-different) | The number of channels, the order of the strings and the interfaces follow from this |
| [Statements that were replaced](#statements-that-were-replaced) | The name and arguments of initialization |
| [What was added](#what-was-added) | Syntax that was originally an error, or was ignored, now has a meaning |
| [What changed](#what-changed) | Written the same way, but takes effect differently |
| [What was removed](#what-was-removed) | Functions that only the built-in FM sound chip and the PSG have |

When you bring over a program written for the original as is, **the first thing to fix is the `CALL MUSIC` line**. From there on, it usually plays as long as it does not use the PSG or the built-in FM sound chip — `CALL MDR` and the MML also work as they are. If it used rhythm, move the rhythm string to the front ("[The sound sources and channels are different](#the-sound-sources-and-channels-are-different)").

## The sound sources and channels are different

| | Original MSX-MIDI BASIC extension | MIDI Play BASIC Extension |
|---|---|---|
| Sound sources it can play | Built-in FM sound chip (OPLL) + PSG + MIDI devices | **MIDI devices only** |
| `PLAY` strings | Up to 13 | **Up to 16** |
| MIDI channels sounding at once | 9 (8 + 1 rhythm when rhythm is used) | **16** (15 + 1 rhythm when rhythm is used) |
| Position of the rhythm string | After the strings for MIDI | **First** |
| MIDI channel for rhythm | No default is stated in the original documentation; specified with `@Hn` | **Default is 10** (can be changed with `@Hn`) |
| MIDI interface | MSX-MIDI | **10 kinds** ([Choosing the interface](#choosing-the-interface)) |

**The PSG and the built-in FM sound chip cannot be played.** The three PSG strings originally placed after `PLAY #1`, and the strings for the built-in FM sound chip in `PLAY #2`, are interpreted as MIDI channels as they are.

Therefore, **the `#<mode>` of `PLAY` has the same meaning whichever of `0`-`3` is written**. Even when it is written, it is skipped, so you can bring `PLAY #1,` over as is. `4` and above give `Illegal function call`, as in the original.

**The rhythm string has moved to the front.** Originally it was placed after the strings for MIDI, and its position was determined by the channel-count arguments of `CALL MUSIC`. Those arguments are gone, so there is no longer anything that determines the position.

```basic
' original               CALL MUSIC(1,0,1,1)  → 1st and 2nd strings are MIDI, 3rd is rhythm
PLAY #1, "CDE", "GAB", "BSH8H8"

' now
CALL MIDI(1)
PLAY "BSH8H8", "@H1CDE", "@H2GAB"
```

---

## Statements that were replaced

### CALL MIDI — initialization

```
CALL MIDI [(<mode> [, <interface number>])]
CALL MIDI(-1)
```

The counterpart of `CALL MUSIC`. **Until this statement initializes, no other BASIC extension statements can be used**, the same as in the original.

| | MSX-MIDI | MIDI Play |
|---|---|---|
| Statement name | `CALL MUSIC` | `CALL MIDI` |
| 1st argument | Mode (0 = without rhythm, 1 = with rhythm) | Same. In addition, **adding `4` times note lengths with the high-precision timer** (below), and **`-1` releases** |
| 2nd argument | `0` (reserved for the built-in FM sound chip) | **Interface number** |
| 3rd and later arguments | Number of channels for each string | **None**. 1 string = 1 MIDI channel |
| Without arguments | Same as `CALL MUSIC(1,0,1,1,1)` | Same as `CALL MIDI(0)` |
| Decrease in memory | 807 bytes | **1912 bytes** |
| Sent at initialization | Not stated in the original documentation | **CC#120 / CC#121 to all 16 channels** |

**The channel-count arguments are gone.** In MIDI, only one MIDI channel is assigned to one string, and even originally these were arguments for which "specifying a value of 2 or more does not change the meaning". As in the original, the correspondence between strings and MIDI channels is changed with `@Hn` in MML.

```basic
CALL MUSIC(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)     ' original
CALL MIDI                     :' now. Nothing to write, whether for 3 strings or 16
```

**It can be released with `CALL MIDI(-1)`.** Originally there was no way to undo initialization. It returns the allocated memory and the interrupt, and goes back to the state before `CALL MIDI` was executed. As with `CALL MUSIC` for initialization, all BASIC variables are cleared after it is executed.

### CALL MDR is unchanged

`CALL MDR(<B>,<S>,<M>,<C>,<H>)` works as in the original, in both how it is written and the order of the arguments. **A way to do the same thing from within MML** has been added, and the initial values have changed.

| | MSX-MIDI | MIDI Play |
|---|---|---|
| How it is written | `CALL MDR(<B>,<S>,<M>,<C>,<H>)` | Same. **In addition, `%<letter>=n;`** (in rhythm MML) |
| Letters that can be assigned | The 5 letters `B` `S` `M` `C` `H` | The same 5 for `CALL MDR`; **the 10 letters `A`-`H` `S` `M`** for `%<letter>=n;` |
| Initial values | All 0 (no sound) | **The GM drum kit** (table below) |
| Omitting arguments | Not possible | Likewise not possible for `CALL MDR` |

| Letter | `B` | `S` | `M` | `C` | `H` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Note number | 36 | 38 | 45 | 49 | 42 |

**Since the initial values are now the GM drum kit, no assignment is needed just to make sound.** Originally the initial values were all 0, and nothing sounded until `CALL MDR` was written.

```basic
' original — nothing sounds until CALL MDR is written
CALL MDR(35, 38, 45, 49, 42)
PLAY #1, "", "", "BSH8H8"

' now — there are three ways to assign
CALL MIDI(1)
PLAY "BSH8H8"                              ' (1) play with the GM defaults as they are
CALL MDR(35,38,45,49,42) : PLAY "BSH8H8"   ' (2) written the same way as in the original
PLAY "%B=35;BSH8H8"                        ' (3) from within MML
```

`CALL MDR` and `%<letter>=n;` rewrite the same place, so whichever is executed later is the one that remains.

**Velocity can also be held per letter.** With `@K<letter>=n;`, you can set the velocity for that percussion instrument alone (default 100). Originally, eight times `Vn` applied to all percussion.

### CALL MUSIC in the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build

**In the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build (the build in the Y8960 cartridge), `CALL MUSIC` has a different meaning.** It is not initialization but a statement that **switches** to another sound BASIC extension on the cartridge. `CALL AUDIO`, `CALL MINIT` and `CALL OPM` are switches of the same form.

**When bringing over a program written for the original, if you forget to remove `CALL MUSIC`, the line you wrote as initialization becomes a "line that goes off elsewhere".**

The standalone cartridge build does not register these four. If another cartridge that has the same name is inserted, that cartridge handles it; otherwise it gives `Syntax error`.

---

## What was added

### Choosing the interface

The original MSX-MIDI BASIC extension could play only MSX-MIDI (the MIDI interface built into the machine). This BASIC extension switches among 10 kinds of interfaces at run time.

Three kinds can be auto-detected: MSX-MIDI, Philips NMS1205 and YAMAHA SFG-01 / SFG-05. For the rest, the MSX has no means to check whether they are present, so name them explicitly with the second argument of `CALL MIDI`. The list of numbers is in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#interface-numbers).

```basic
CALL MIDI(0, 8)      ' BIT2 MIDI Saurus (port A)
```

**How it sounds differs in some respects depending on the interface**: whether short note lengths can be timed, and whether MIDI clock is sent. These are summarized in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#differences-between-interfaces).

### Choosing the playback tick

Originally, the playback tick was fixed at 1/60 second. In addition, this BASIC extension can make the tick from the interface's **high-precision timer**. Adding `4` to the `CALL MIDI` mode switches to it.

```basic
CALL MIDI      :' 1/60 second (same as the original)
CALL MIDI(4)   ' high-precision timer
```

Timing with the high-precision timer **plays 96th notes at any tempo and sends MIDI clock**. In exchange, BASIC slows down by the amount of the added interrupts. **The default is 1/60 second**, so if you write as in the original, it plays with the same tick as the original. For details, see [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#the-playback-tick).

### Velocity can be written in 127 steps

Originally, velocity could be set only with `Vn` (1-15) and the rhythm `@An` (0-15), and in both cases the value sent was 8 times that. Only multiples of 8 could be sent.

| | MSX-MIDI | MIDI Play |
|---|---|---|
| Per note | None | **`<note name>[<length>],n` (0-127)** |
| Value when omitted | 8 times `Vn` | **`@Kn` (0-127, default 100)**. `Vn` also remains |
| Rhythm accent | 8 times `@An` (0-15) | **`@An` (0-127, default 127)** |
| Normal rhythm sounds | 8 times `Vn` | **`@K<letter>=n;` (0-127, default 100)** |

```basic
PLAY "@K80 O4CDE C4,120"     ' the first 3 notes are 80, only the last C is 120
```

`Vn` keeps both its notation and sending 8 times the value, as in the original, so `V8` and the like work as they are. Only the lower limit of the range has widened, to `0` ("[Lower limits of numbers](#lower-limits-of-numbers)").

### Commands for expression

Things that were "×" in the original implementation chart, and things for which you had to write the control change number yourself, now have names.

| Command | Contents | Original |
|---|---|---|
| `Pn` `@Pn` (-1200 to 1200) | Pitch bend. The unit is cents | × |
| `&` | Tie / legato. Sends CC#68 | Only joins notes |
| `~[n]` (0-127) | Portamento. Sends CC#65 / CC#84 | None |
| `@En` (0-127) | Expression (CC#11) | `@C11,n` |
| `@In` (0-127) | Panning (CC#10) | `@C10,n` |
| `@Mn` (0-127) | Modulation (CC#1) | `@C1,n` |

`&` is a command that existed in the original, and its role of joining notes has not changed. The difference is that **it now sends legato on / off (CC#68) before and after the joined section**.

In GM2, `&` and `~` are guaranteed to work only in mono mode. Send `@C126,1` before using them.

The pitch bend width is determined by a setting on the sound source side (bend range). The default is 2 semitones, and when it is changed with `@R0,n`, pitch bend follows it.

### Commands that send raw MIDI data

| Command | Contents | Original |
|---|---|---|
| `@m,l,p` | Program change with bank select | None |
| `@Nr,d` `@Nm,l,d` | NRPN | None |
| `@Rr,d` `@Rm,l,d` | RPN | None |

The original also had `@Cm,n` and `Zn`, so the same thing could be sent by lining up the bytes. `@N` / `@R` take care of splitting the 14-bit number into MSB / LSB.

```basic
PLAY "@N1054,64"       ' same as @C99,8 @C98,30 @C6,64
```

### Extensions to MML notation

These were added in MSX-MUSIC BASIC Extension V2 and can be used as they are.

| Form | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$` followed by 2 hexadecimal digits | `O$04` is `O4`, `@C$07,$40` is `@C7,64` |
| Length `0` (`C0`) | Issues only a note-on and consumes no time |
| `R0` | Issues only a note-off and consumes no time |
| `R.` | Dotted rest |

```basic
PLAY "T120O4C0@W8P100@W8P200@W8R0"     ' move the pitch within 1 note
```

### @Wn and @Sn in rhythm MML

`@Wn` and `@Sn`, which were not in the original rhythm MML table, can also be written in rhythm MML. Their meaning is the same as in melody MML.

Rhythm MML has no `Ln`, so **omitting the length of `@Wn` waits for the length of a quarter note**.

```basic
CALL MIDI(1)
PLAY "@S1BSH8H8@W2"     ' send Start, then wait for the length of a half note
```

---

## What changed

### Tempo

**`Tn` now takes effect on all strings, whichever string it is written in**. Originally, each string (part) had its own tempo, and the tempo of the MIDI clock was defined as "the same as the 1st string". In this BASIC extension, a `T` written at the start of the first string takes effect on all strings, so you do not need to write it in each string as you did originally.

Programs that played strings at different tempos sound different. Programs that changed the tempo in the middle of a piece by writing `T` at the same position in all strings may also find that the position of the change shifts in the other strings (the description of `T` in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#mml-list)).

### MIDI clock

The notation of `@S0` / `@S1` / `@S2` and the status bytes they send (`FCh` / `FAh` / `FBh`) are unchanged from the original. How the clock is output is different.

| | MSX-MIDI | MIDI Play |
|---|---|---|
| When the clock is output | After `@S1` / `@S2`, **only while `PLAY` is running** | After `@S1` / `@S2`. It keeps being output even after `PLAY` ends |
| When the clock stops | When `PLAY` ends (`FCh` is not sent) | `@S0`, `CALL MIDI(-1)`, or running `CALL MIDI` again (the latter two **send `FCh`**) |
| Clock tempo | The 1st string of `PLAY` | The tempo of the whole piece |
| Differences between interfaces | None | **Yes**. The clock is output only while timing with the high-precision timer (when `4` is added to the mode of `CALL MIDI` and the interface has a high-precision timer). Otherwise only the signal status bytes are output |

So that a receiver that has been started is not left running on its own, `CALL MIDI(-1)` and running `CALL MIDI` again send Stop. This is because both stop the clock. Once the clock has been stopped with `@S0`, they do not send it.

### Messages sent

This does not change how the result sounds, but the bytes on the wire are different.

| | MSX-MIDI | MIDI Play |
|---|---|---|
| Note-off | `9nH` + velocity 0 | **`8nH` + velocity 0** |
| Rhythm note-off | Sent (simultaneous notes use running status) | **Not sent** (GM specifies that it is ignored on the rhythm channel) |
| Running status | Used for rhythm | **Not used** |
| At initialization | Not stated in the original documentation | **CC#120 (All Sound Off) and CC#121 (Reset All Controllers) to all 16 channels** |

### Lower limits of numbers

Arguments that originally started at `1` now start at `0`. The upper limits do not change.

| Command | MSX-MIDI | MIDI Play |
|---|---|---|
| `@n` | 1-127 | 0-127 |
| `@Vn` | 1-127 | 0-127 |
| `Vn` | 1-15 | 0-15 |
| `Zn` | 1-255 | 0-255 |

### Upper limit of tuplet and rhythm lengths

The n of tuplet `{ }n` and the lengths in rhythm MML **can be written up to 96**. In the original documentation both were up to 64, and the original documentation does not state whether these two were also extended when the original MSX-MIDI BASIC extension extended `Ln` `Rn` `@Wn` to 96.

### Rests inside tuplets

Tuplet `{ }n` counts `R` as one note as well. Originally, only that `R` remained a quarter rest, so the total of the tuplet did not add up. Now an `R` with its length omitted takes the tuplet length.

```basic
PLAY "T60{CDR}1"      ' R is a third rest, the same as C and D. A whole note in total
PLAY "T60{CDR12}1"    ' A written length wins. Same as originally
PLAY "T60R"           ' R outside a tuplet is still a quarter rest. Same as originally
```

An `R` with its length written and an `R` outside a tuplet do not change.

### PLAY with several strings built by expressions

Originally, when 2 or more strings built by concatenation or functions were lined up in `PLAY`, an earlier string could be overwritten by the contents of a later string, and MML different from what was written could play. Now each plays as written.

```basic
A$="E4"
PLAY "O4C4"+A$, "O4D4"+A$    ' Originally the 1st string also played D and E. Now C and E
```

In exchange, **strings built by expressions are limited to 10 per `PLAY` statement**. Lining up 11 or more gives `String formula too complex`. String constants and string variables are not counted.

---

## What was removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **The built-in FM sound chip and PSG** | This BASIC extension plays only MIDI. The meaning of `#<mode>` in `PLAY`, the channel-count arguments and the strings for PSG are all gone |
| **`Sn` (envelope shape)** | A PSG feature. Writing it gives `Illegal function call` |
| **`Mn` (envelope period)** | Same as above |
| **`Yr,d` (register write)** | A feature of the built-in FM sound chip and PSG. Rhythm MML has no `Yr,d` either |
| **`Zn` in rhythm MML** | Originally it could also be written in rhythm MML. Now it gives `Illegal function call`. `Zn` in melody MML does not change |
| **`CALL PLAY`** | Gets the playback state. Its name is not registered at all |

`CALL AUDREG`, `CALL PITCH`, `CALL TEMPER`, `CALL TRANSPOSE` and `CALL VOICE`, which were originally described as "having no meaning for MIDI devices", **do not have their names registered at all** in this BASIC extension. If another cartridge that has the same names is inserted, it handles them as before; if not, they give `Syntax error`.

---

## What has not changed

MML, except that for rhythm, can be used as it is.

- Notes, rests (except inside tuplets; "[Rests inside tuplets](#rests-inside-tuplets)"), octaves, `Qn`, `Nn`, `.`, `{ }n` (for the upper limit, "[Upper limit of tuplet and rhythm lengths](#upper-limit-of-tuplet-and-rhythm-lengths)")
- The upper limit of 96 for lengths (`Ln` `Rn` `@Wn` and the lengths attached to notes)
- The range `O1C` (note number 24)-`O8B` (119). `O4C` is 60
- `@Hn` (1-16), `@Cm,n`, `@Vn`, `Vn` (`n*8`), `Zn`, `@Sn` (for the lower limits of `@Vn` `Vn` `Zn`, "[Lower limits of numbers](#lower-limits-of-numbers)")
- Setting parameters from variables with `=x;`, and playing string variables with `Xx;`
- The notation of rhythm MML (`<letter>[!]...<length>`) and the meaning of `!`
- MIDI is not received

Apart from initialization, statements also keep the same names and arguments.

- `CALL BGM`, `CALL STOPM`, `CALL MDR`
- The `PLAY` statement itself
